newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end slightly firmer ahead of break.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end slightly firmer ahead of break.

text.p: Italian stocks closed generally higher helped up by lira and bond market strength on Thursday, with trade thin ahead of a three-day weekend beginning Friday,
The blue-chip Mib30 index closed 0.37 percent up at 14452 while the all-share Mibtel stood 0.4 percent higher at 9626.
Total volume reached 460 billion lire, of which some 120 billion lire was entirely down to trading on shares in state-controlled energy group Eni.

Mobile phone group TIM climbed 3.19 percent to 3135 lire per ordinary share. Buyers were encouraged by results for the first nine months of this year. TIM's digital GSM service had an operating result of just over 100 billion lire.
TIM also decided to buy from its parent state telecoms holding Stet a 49 percent stake in Stet Mobile Holding, giving it a potential foothold in the French mobile phone market.
Stet itself was buffeted by various developments and eventually ended down 0.81 percent at 5259 lire.
Managing director Ernesto Pascale was placed under investigation in a corruption probe in the north west Italian town of Aosta.

In the saga of stalled draft legislation to create a watchdog for Italy's telecoms and broadcasting sectors, the far-right National Alliance party said it was withdrawing obstructionist amendments to the bill.
Meanwhile a far-left Communist Refoundation economic spokesman said an agreement between the government and the hard left could be found on creating a telecom authority.
The spokeman said the two camps' positions were not irreconcilable and latest Treasury suggestions were alright.
Creation of a watchdog is essential to the privatisation of Stet, which the government wants to carry out before March 31 next year.
State energy company ENI continues to attract high turnover although it ended at odds with the overall market, down 0.07 percent at 7256 lire, traders said.
The Milan stock market is closed on Friday and trading resumes on Monday.
